selected_question: Optimal information cost of local real-time thermal response prediction from noisy scalar imaginary-time correlations, with a local microscopic lower family and matching recovery.
status: Complete analytic theorem and finite represented constructions at the specified observation-channel contract.
main_law: At beta=Omega=variance=1, error 1/64, success 2/3, N<=ceil(T)+1: log(1+M_star(T))=Theta(T log(2+T)).
source_class: Open nearest-neighbor XY spin chains; A=X_1; positive one-particle Jacobi spectrum in [Omega/2,Omega]; explicitly counted sites.
microscopic_encoding: Rational onsite coefficients and explicit positive square roots of rational squared hoppings. O(n^3 log n) description bits at fixed beta,Omega; polynomial-bit constructor.
observations: Chosen tau in [0,beta]; independent Gaussian additive noise of known variance per scalar reading. Adaptive queries allowed in lower bound; fixed worst-case query budget.
output: Finite polynomial record for R(t)=-Im C(it), uniform on [0,T], with a simultaneous confidence certificate.
granted_side_information: Site count, structural class, transition band; lower pair also shares exact one-particle frequencies, compact subset-sum many-body spectrum and all partition functions.

acquisition_cost: All (m+1)r readings counted; settings, readout digits, clipping, time/temperature calibration, and processing costs explicit. Huge schedules not executed.
known_source_comparator: Given actual J, finite matrix methods compute tanh(beta J/2)sin(tJ) in polynomial bit work at fixed bandwidth/temperature. This is not full-Hamiltonian hardness.

resource_holds: No new worker, researcher, descendant, local team, infrastructure, hardware, spend, experiment or outreach. P1/P3 undisturbed, Sol closed/held, Dots unmessaged.
